title: Export Finance and Insurance Corporation Amendment (New Mandate and Other Measures) Bill 2013

speeches.speaker: Kelvin Thomson
speeches.brief: Introduced the EFIC bill implementing the government's response, announced in January, to the 2012 Productivity Commission report on export credit arrangements, and said that consistent with the 2003 Uhrig review, a government member will be removed from EFIC's board to increase its independence.

speeches.speaker: Julie Bishop
speeches.brief: Noted this is the second Export Finance and Insurance Corporation bill before parliament this year, recalling that the previous bill extracted a $200 million special dividend from EFIC's reserves to help plug the government's budget shortfall.

speeches.speaker: Craig Kelly
speeches.brief: Supported the bill's principles but questioned its market failure test, arguing Australian small business exporters already face higher finance costs from the four major banks than overseas competitors, and cited the Community Energy Efficiency Program as a hypocritical example where council-run swimming pools can get carbon tax relief grants but competing private pools cannot.

speeches.speaker: Kelvin Thomson
speeches.brief: Thanked the opposition for supporting the EFIC bill, but rejected the member for Hughes's description of Australia's carbon price as the world's highest as a tired and incorrect claim.
